item.text:
Continued. The latest result turns F17 from a table inconsistency into an executed ordering violation.

`TestAuditPrepareReplyConflictMiss` recovers a committed PUT on key 66 at instance 2.0, then proposes a new PUT on the same key. Because recovery did not update the conflict table, the new proposal's dependency vector is empty:

```
new proposal deps=[-1 -1 -1 -1 -1] (recovered instance is 2.0)
new proposal deps[2]=-1, want 0; it misses the recovered committed key
```

The proposal therefore does not depend on the recovered committed instance, creating the same class of ordering violation as the batched-dependency defect.

The critical F1 result also now includes an all-alive state-machine divergence: with a partitioned leader, recovery commits NOOP on replicas 1-4, the healed leader 0 retains the chosen PUT, and executing the instance gives key 7 only on replica 0.

Current status: four cluster controls pass; 29 finding tests fail as intended; `go build ./...` passes; the captured implementation remains byte-identical to `../source`.
